artifacts.summary: All six plan phases completed: --only flag in run-all.sh, suite-selection-lib.sh mapping library, regression suite, and real-battery acceptance measurement with honest wall-clock figures and a corrected failure characterization.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a strictly opt-in --only SUITE[,SUITE,...] flag to run-all.sh plus a new sourced-only scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh mapping library (three-strata touched-file -> suite resolution with a fail-safe full-sweep sentinel), a 15-case regression suite, and manifest.json registration. Proved the strict-subset property and a ~49% wall-clock reduction on a representative selection against the real battery under heavy concurrent host load, with Gate 8's own full sweep left unchanged by default.

memory_candidates.content: A regression suite that hardcodes a specific real-corpus basename as a literal quoted string (e.g. to pick a known 'zero-reference' fixture file) self-poisons the very fixture it tests once the suite itself exists in the corpus: a grep-based reference-lookup mechanism scanning all suite source text will find the suite's own quoted string as a 'reference' to that basename. Fix: derive the fixture candidate dynamically at test runtime (scan the live corpus, pick the first candidate with zero grep hits including against the new suite's own file) instead of hardcoding a name -- also more robust to corpus drift than a frozen name.

git-commit-scoped.sh's git add always re-reads the full working-tree file content (no partial-hunk staging). If a concurrent sibling task has simultaneously added its own additive-only lines to the same shared file (e.g. a manifest.json array) that this task also needs to add a line to, committing the pathspec directly sweeps the sibling's uncommitted work into this task's commit under the wrong provenance. Procedure: (1) snapshot the current working-tree file; (2) temporarily remove the sibling's lines (identified via git diff against HEAD) so only this task's own hunk remains as a diff from HEAD; (3) commit via git-commit-scoped.sh normally; (4) immediately restore the sibling's lines into the (still-uncommitted) working tree from the snapshot, verified via diff. Works cleanly when both edits are additive-only lines in the same array with no overlapping modifications.
